gloss: to see off; to postpone; to let pass

definitions.gloss: to see off; to bid farewell
definitions.explanation: To accompany someone to their departure point and watch them leave.
To decide not to proceed with something at this time.

definitions.gloss: to let pass; to pass on
definitions.explanation: To deliberately not take action on an opportunity.

examples.japanese: {空港|くうこう}まで{友人|ゆうじん}を{見送|みおく}りに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to the airport to see my friend off.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}の{計画|けいかく}は{見送|みおく}ることになった。
examples.english: It was decided to shelve this plan.

examples.japanese: バッターは{見逃|みのが}しの{三振|さんしん}で{打席|だせき}を{見送|みおく}った。
examples.english: The batter struck out looking without swinging.

notes:
{見送|みおく}る is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) formed from {見|み}る (to see) + {送|おく}る (to send off). It has both literal and figurative meanings.

ASPECT (ている):
{見送|みおく}っている indicates the ongoing action of watching someone leave, or that something has been put on hold.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [person]を{見送|みおく}る — to see [person] off
- [plan/opportunity]を{見送|みおく}る — to postpone/pass on [plan/opportunity]

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {駅|えき}まで{見送|みおく}る (see off to the station)
- {購入|こうにゅう}を{見送|みおく}る (postpone purchasing)
- {今回|こんかい}は{見送|みおく}る (pass on this opportunity)

BUSINESS/FORMAL USE:
{見送|みおく}る is commonly used in business contexts to mean declining or postponing something politely.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見|み}つめる: to stare at, gaze at (different meaning)
- {見逃|みのが}す: to overlook, miss
